description: A free Chromium browser for the Mac: Arc's sidebar, Dia's polish. Chat on Discord: discord.gg/TdhuXrbcA6

latest_release.name: Ardia 0.2.48
latest_release.body:
## New

- **Passkeys from iCloud Keychain.** Apple granted Ardia the browser passkey entitlement, so sites can offer the passkeys saved in your iCloud Keychain, the same ones Safari and your iPhone use. When a site saves a passkey you choose Ardia's own passkeys or Passwords (iCloud Keychain), and the first time a site uses them, macOS asks whether Ardia may. Settings › Engines › Passkeys shows the status and opens System Settings if it's off. Security keys, phone sign-in and Touch ID passkeys work as before.
- **iCloud Passwords works in Ardia.** Apple approved Ardia, so Apple's iCloud Passwords extension can now reach the Passwords app: add it from the Chrome Web Store and macOS asks to enable Password AutoFill for Ardia. The Apple Passwords plugin is gone. If you used it, Ardia's own passwords take over again, with Offer to save passwords turned back on.
- **Pages in WebKit get what Chromium pages have.** A site that opens in WebKit now fills your saved passwords, addresses and cards (only on the site they belong to), offers to save a sign-in after it succeeds, shows its notifications through Ardia, blocks ads and trackers as strictly as Chromium does (your own uBlock Origin filters included), refuses certificate errors it can't safely bypass and honours HSTS, and has find, view source, save page and Developer Tools.
- **Your sign-in comes along when a site switches engines.** Moving a site between Chromium and WebKit carries its cookies and saved site data both ways, so you stay signed in. Private windows and sites that block cookies carry nothing. Settings › Advanced › Bring sign-ins along turns it off.
- **Plugins can add more to the browser.** A plugin can now add commands to the command bar, a view in the sidebar, a panel beside the page, a toolbar button with a popover and an address-bar keyword, all drawn in Ardia's own style. Plugins still arrive off and ask first. The consent sheet lists each permission separately, including the exact websites a plugin may reach, and plugins never run in private windows. Mac only for now.
- **The profile switcher is one switch.** Settings › Profiles › "Show the profile switcher in the sidebar" replaces Dots, Icons and Nothing. Each profile is a dot unless you gave it an icon: right-click a dot › Add Icon…, or Settings › Profiles › Icon, and Remove turns it back into a dot. Onboarding no longer asks "Dots or icons?". Nothing changes on update: a switcher that showed dots, icons or nothing still does.
- **Edit any theme colour.** Pick one of the nine colours in Settings › Profiles › Theme, the New Tab page's Make it yours panel or onboarding, and the editor opens on it. Your changes stay with that colour when you switch away and back, and Reset puts it back as it came. The separate Custom swatch is gone: a custom theme you already had becomes your edit of the colour it was on, and looks exactly as before.
- **Picture choices in Settings.** Settings › Appearance › Switching tabs shows what ⌃Tab does as two cards, Step through tabs and Recent tabs switcher, so people coming from Arc can get the switcher back in one click. If your own shortcuts match neither, it says Custom and links to them. The address bar's place, what ⌘L opens and hiding the toolbar while scrolling are picture cards too.
- **One switch for programs that control Ardia.** Settings › Advanced › Command line and automation has "Let programs control Ardia", for the `ardia` command and any plugin that drives the browser. Turning it off stays off: a restart, or installing a plugin that wants control, leaves it off, and the plugin tells you where to turn it on. The Command Line plugin is now an ordinary plugin, using the same extension points any plugin can.

## Fixed

- **Hide Element can no longer be started or steered by a page; rules it saved are checked on update.**
- **Shortcuts keep working after you leave a password field.** Switching to another app while a web page's password field had focus could leave macOS's sec

detail.readme:
Touch grass.

Arc’s sidebar and Dia’s polish on real Chromium.
Free and open source. Ads and trackers stay out.

Download Ardia 0.2.48 for Mac

134 MB DMG · macOS 14 Sonoma or later · Apple Silicon · Notarized by Apple
Like your paint wet? The nightly has every fix the day it’s made, smudges and all.
Homebrew: brew install ardia-browser/tap/ardia
On your phone: iPhone (TestFlight) · Android (APK)
ardia.dev · What’s new · All releases · Discord

## Lose the toolbar. Move the address bar into the sidebar and the page runs all the way to the top of the window. ## Two pages, one window. Drag a tab onto the page. Up to three panes, side by side or stacked. ## Refuses to leave the picture. Switch tabs mid-video and it floats along in the corner. Go back to its tab and it slips back into the page. ## Your extensions come along. The Chrome Web Store just works, its button says Add to Ardia, and Sync takes them to your other Macs. ## Ads and trackers stay out. The full uBlock Origin is built in, cookie banners included. Google’s pings are compiled out. Crash reports are opt-in and never carry your sites or searches. ## Also in there - **Work stays at work.** Each profile keeps its own logins, history, extensions and colour. Swipe the sidebar to switch. - **Little Ardia.** ⌥⌘N opens a small window with one page and no sidebar. - **Groups on contact.** Drop a tab on a tab and they’re a group, named for you. - **Moves in for you.** Bookmarks, history, passwords and logins from Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Arc, Dia and five more. Arc’s spaces, pinned tabs and themes too. - **Paints like Arc.** Gradient themes per profile: up to three colours, some grain, some blur. - **Syncs through your iCloud.** End-to-end encrypted, in a folder in your own iCloud Drive. No server of ours in the middle. - **Command bar.** ⌘L finds tabs, history and bookmarks, does your sums, and knows doc.new and 16 friends. - **Tidies up.** ⌥⌘K sweeps the tabs you haven’t touched into Recently Cleaned. - **Clean links.** Copy a link and the tracking junk stays behind. - **Naps when you do.** Background tabs past your latest five freeze, and sleep after half an hour. - **Sits still.** Idles under half a percent of CPU with a tab open. - **Updates itself.** Quietly, then shows you what changed. ## It’s actually Chromium. Not WebKit. Not Electron. Every window is Chrome’s own, so sites, extensions and DevTools behave like they do in Chrome. | Part | Details | Status | | --- | --- | --- | | Engine | Chromium 158, on Chrome’s own framework. | ✓ Yes | | De-Googled | Google’s background services stripped out. | ✓ Yes | | H.264 and AAC | The codecs Chromium leaves out. | ✓ Yes | | DevTools | Docked, with device mode. Like Chrome. | ✓ Yes | | Sync | End-to-end encrypted, through your own iCloud Drive. | ✓ Yes | | Translate | On your Mac. Nothing leaves it. | ✓ macOS 26 | | Passkeys | Touch ID and iCloud Keychain. | ~ Partly | | Netflix and DRM | Streaming sites open in WebKit, where they play. Widevine in Chromium waits on Google. | ~ Partly | | Intel Macs | Apple Silicon only. | ✗ No |

Download Ardia 0.2.48

It’s 134 MB and one drag into Applications.
Not on a Mac? Watch › Custom › Releases up top and GitHub tells you when it is.

--- # Build it yourself A macOS browser that looks and feels like [Dia](https://diabrowser.com): Chrome's own framework from our patched Chromium with our layer on top (ArdiaCore), an Expo + React Native macOS shell, and Metal shaders reconstructed from Dia's own New Tab effects. ``` apps/ browser/ Expo + react-native-macos app (UI in src/, Xcode project in macos/) linux/ Linux desktop entry, window controls and native host integration; shares the browser UI packages/ ardiacore/ The engine: Chromium 158's framework with our layer (Chrome tabs hosted in our views), JS API in src/ shell/ Native menu bar + shortcuts → JS, windows, SF Symbols, native primitives shaders/ Metal: New Tab effects + grained OKLab window backdrop import/ Import from other browsers (bookmarks, history, passwords, Arc spaces) core/ Pure TS: omnibox input → URL, suggestions, Dia-style breadcrumbs (tested) ``` ## Run it The Linux desktop target is `apps/desktop`, for x86-64 Linux on Wayland or X11. Releases ship it as a `.deb` (`sudo apt install ./Ardia--linux-x64.deb`), an AppImage, a tarball and an Arch source package, and stables as `ardia-bin` on the AUR: [docs/linux-port.md › Installing on Linux](docs/linux-port.md#installing-on-linux). The same file has the source-build and packaging instructions. It builds against the dedicated Linux Chromium host. The macOS app requires Xcode 26+, CocoaPods, Node 24 (pinned in `.nvmrc`), pnpm 12. ```bash pnpm install ``` The engine (Chrome's framework, built from our patched Chromium) comes prebuilt: with no local engine build, the app's build downloads the one matching your checkout's macOS engine key (`engine/engine-key.sh --platform macos`; about 110 MB, once; Apple Silicon only) and checks it against `packages/ardiacore/prebuilt-engines.tsv`. Every release whose engine changed publishes one. If `main`'s engine is newer than the last release's, work from a release tag (`v0.2.30`, say), or run `packages/ardiacore/scripts/fetch-engine.sh --nearest` to build against the newest prebuilt anyway. Passkeys and saved cards need our team ID and won't work in a build signed by anyone else. To change the engine itself (anything under `engine/`), build it from source: Chrome's framework from our patched Chromium tree in `~/chromium-build` (Chromium 158.0.8127.36 with the patch series in `engine/patches`; `docs/engine-build.md` › "Rebuilding", then `engine/chromium/apply.sh`, `engine/ardiacore/apply.sh` and `autoninja -C out/Release_GN_arm64 chrome_framework`; the first build takes about 2 hours). The app's build stages it from there when it exists. ```bash pnpm pods ``` In one terminal, start Metro: ```bash pnpm dev ``` In another, build and launch the Debug app (on its own data, `~/Library/Application Support/Ardia Dev`, or `ARDIA_DATA_DIR`): ```bash pnpm macos ``` Other tasks: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm shaders:check` (compiles the embedded Metal offline), `scripts/agent/build-app --config Release` (a Release `.app` with a Hermes bytecode bundle in `apps/browser/build-`, under the shared build locks; `--help`). Signed releases (DMG, Sparkle zip and appcast) are built by the Release workflow with `scripts/release.sh`, see `docs/releasing.md`. Shortcuts: ⌘T new tab, ⌘L command bar, ⌘W close, ⇧⌘T reopen, ⌘S sidebar, ⌘[ / ⌘] back/forward, ⌘R reload, ⌘1–⌘9 select tab, ⌃Tab cycle. ## How Dia's New Tab light works Dia 1.50 turns this light off along with its rebrand (a painted mark, a single-colour power-up band and a halo around the bar; `docs/dia-spec.md` › "1.50 Sunglow"), and so does Ardia. The reconstruction left the tree with it: `git show f2c0e251:packages/shaders/ios/AreaLightView.swift`. These findings come from disassembling the Metal libraries in `Dia.app` (v1.49.1) with `xcrun metal-objdump`. `BoostBrowser_PowerUp.bundle/default.metallib` contains `breathingAreaLightFragment`, which the Swift class `NewTabPage.NewTabAreaLightView` hosts. The reconstruction was `AreaLightView.swift` (above). - **The command bar is a light source.** Dia models the bar as a rounded-rectangle area light floating `lift` points above the page. Each pixel receives the closed-form irradiance of that rectangle: the solid-angle formula, one `atan` term per corner, times 1/2π. Rounded corners subtract (1 − π/4) of each corner square. The result is a physically correct penumbra: a higher lift gives a softer, wider glow. - **Falloff** is reshaped from inverse-square to `(h/d)^falloff`, where `d` is the distance to the emitter's rounded-rect surface rather than to its centre. - **Colour** is Dia's brand spectrum (`ProgressBarColor2…7` in its asset catalog): blue `#0358F7`, steel `#5092C7`, lavender `#E1E1FE`, yellow `#FFD400`, orange `#FA3D1D` and magenta `#FD02F5`. It is laid out as a wrapping, slightly diagonal gradient that scrolls every 20 s. IQ's 2D simplex noise warps the gradient under the bar, and the warp fades out into the penumbra. - **Dark mode** treats the light as HDR emission and applies the Hable/Uncharted-2 filmic tonemap (white point 11.2), with alpha set to Rec.709 luminance. **Light mode** keeps the flat palette colour and uses the irradiance as opacity. - **Finishing:** alpha fades over the top 50 pt and bottom 200 pt of the view, and ±3/255 triangular dither (Dave Hoskins' `hash12`) prevents banding in the long soft falloff. - **Animation:** the shader itself only scrolls the colours. The lift-off intro and the slow "breathing" come from the CPU, which animates `lift` and `intensity`. Those curves live in Dia's Swift code, so the ones here (quartic ease-out over 1.1 s, ±7% intensity on a 5.5 s sine) are my approximation. The **window backdrop** comes from `ARC_WindowThemeUI.bundle` (`gradientFragment` + `renderFragment`). Gradient stops are stored and mixed in **OKLab**, then converted to linear sRGB and gamma-encoded in the shader. A tiled grain texture is then multiply-blended on top. `WindowBackdropView` does the same with procedural grain. Only math and colour values are reused. No Dia images, fonts or binaries are copied into this repo. ## Architecture notes - **Why Expo SDK 54:** `react-native-macos` tops out at 0.81, which pairs with Expo SDK 54 (whose `ExpoAppDelegate` / `ExpoReactNativeFactory` have macOS code paths). - **Legacy architecture.** react-native-macos 0.81's Fabric support is experimental, so the app runs on the legacy architecture. One consequence: Expo's legacy view-manager adapter instantiates a module's *first* view class for every view it declares, so each native view has its own module. - **Metro, not `expo start`.** Metro runs through the react-native-macos CLI. `metro.config.js` redirects `react-native` → `react-native-macos` for `platform=macos`, because defining our own `resolveRequest` replaces the redirect the CLI would install. - **No Reanimated.** It has no macOS build for 0.81; animations use RN's `Animated`. - **Monorepo paths.** pnpm is set to `nodeLinker: hoisted` because CocoaPods and Metro resolve `react-native-macos` by path. The Podfile rewrites `REACT_NATIVE_PATH` to the hoisted location and raises every pod's deployment target to 14.0, since Xcode 26+ rejects the 11.0 some Expo pods declare. - **Native subviews** are sized in `setFrameSize`, not `layout()`. RN macOS assigns frames directly and never autoresizes subviews. - **Shaders** are Metal source embedded in Swift and compiled at runtime (once per class, cached). This keeps the pods free of a metallib build phase. ## Status Feature parity with Dia (everything but its AI) is tracked row by row in [docs/dia-feature-parity.md](docs/dia-feature-parity.md); releases and their notes are at [ardia.dev/release-notes](https://ardia.dev/release-notes). ## Sponsors Greptile reads every pull request before we do. [Blacksmith](https://www.blacksmith.sh) runs our CI. Monthly donors who asked to be listed are on [ardia.dev](https://ardia.dev/#sponsors). [Chip in](https://ardia.dev/#donate) to join them. ## License Ardia as distributed is licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3](LICENSE), because its engine is built with GPL-3.0 patches. Ardia's own source files are under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE.Apache-2.0). It builds on Chromium, carries a few of the Chromium Embedded Framework's patches to Chromium (BSD-3-Clause), and bundles uBlock Origin, each under its own license; see [NOTICE](NOTICE). Every release links its source.
